description: The outcome of a set of mechanical checks over one primary subject, with each check's attempts recorded in order so a flake is distinguishable from a pass.

body/conclusion.label: Conclusion
body/conclusion.description: Recomputed from the checks and rejected unless it matches exactly. The producer writes it and has no say in it.

body/checks.label: Checks
body/checks.description: A record with no checks is valid and concludes incomplete.

body/checks/*/attempts.label: Attempts
body/checks/*/attempts.description: An array and not an entity-set: attempts have no id, so no stored address can name one. They are identified only by their position, and position is not an address.

body/checks/*/attempts/*/status.description: Narrower than a check's status: an attempt cannot be skipped, because a skipped check has no attempts.

body/checks/*/attempts/*/duration.label: Duration
body/checks/*/attempts/*/duration.description: Nothing times the attempt independently; this is the producer's own measurement, constrained only in syntax and sign.

go_only_rules.rule: The conclusion is derived from the checks and must match exactly: any check in error yields error; otherwise any failed check yields failed; otherwise any skipped check, or no checks at all, yields incomplete; otherwise passed.
A skipped check must have no attempts; a passed, failed or error check requires at least one.
Each attempt's number must equal its position in the array plus one, with no exception, so the field is pinned rather than chosen.
A check with attempts must carry the status of its final attempt.
Attempts are addressable only in declaration paths. Reordering them would repoint any position-based reference, which is why none exists.
An anchor's subject must name a subject this record declares.

The locator kind decides which locator fields must be present and forbids the rest: file-lines and log-lines require a canonical relative path with a positive start and an end at or after it; byte-range requires a path with a nonnegative start and an end strictly after it; json-pointer requires a valid non-root JSON pointer alone; opaque requires a value alone.
Nothing verifies that an anchor points at anything. Anchor content hashes are deferred, so every locator detail is a producer claim.
